newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen shares fall at noon, confidence shaken.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares fall at noon, confidence shaken.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B shares fell sharply at midday on Monday and sentiment deteriorated as the disappointing performance of both indices since the Hong Kong handover on July 1 continued to shake confidence, brokers said.
The domestic A shares plunged 15.89 points or 3.86 percent to 395.74 points on turnover of 2.2 billion yuan.
The foreign currency B index tumbled 4.90 points or 3.62 percent to 130.50 points on thin turnover of HK$17 million.

Brokers said they expected shares to fall further in the afternoon, extending the bearish mood that has prevailed since Hong Kong's transition to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 failed to inspire the market.
"Investor confidence has been eroded by our market's worse-than-expected performance since the Hong Kong handover," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Shares lost heavily on rumours of new anti-speculation measures as well as talk that securities authorities planned to increase supervision over listed firms' interim reports.
Any tightening would work to stop listed firms exaggerating their profits, an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Listed firms must release their 1997 first-half reports by the end of August.
Livzon Pharmaceutical was Monday morning's biggest B share loser, falling HK$0.44 or 9.80 percent to HK$4.05.
On the A share market, property developer Shenzhen Fountain dropped 1.49 yuan to its 10 percent limit-down at 13.41 yuan as the session's worst performer.
